candidate_windows.window_text: We now describe the datasets, models,and parameters used in our experiments.

We consider models from different providers and sizes.

Smallmodels,namelyGemma-2-9B-it $( \mathsf { G E M } _ { \mathsf { S } } )$ ，Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct $( \mathsf { L A M } _ { s } )$ ，and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 $( \mathsf { M S T } _ { \mathsf { S } } )$ ).

Medium models,consist of Gemma-2-27B-it $\left( \mathsf { G E M } _ { \mathsf { m } } \right)$ ，Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct $( \mathsf { L A M } _ { \mathsf { m } } )$ ，and Mistral-Small-24B-Instruct-2501 $( \mathsf { M S T } _ { \mathsf { m } } )$ .

Reasoningmodel. Weonlyconsider DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B $\left( \mathsf { R } 1 _ { \mathsf { m } } \right)$

All experiments were run on a single node with $8 \mathrm { { x } }$ NVIDIA H20O GPUs.The machine was shared between multiple research teams.We ran all the models in 32-bit precision and did not employ any size reduction strategies like quantization. We considered two temperature values, $T = 0$ and $T = 0 . 5$ . For unconstrained and rationale-based prompting at $T = 0 . 5$ ，we ran five trials and reported the mean for all metrics. Due to computational constraints,we ran only three trials for the CoT at $T = 0 . 5$

For generating the counterfactuals, we provided the model with the target label $y _ { \mathrm { C E } }$ . For classification datasets,we selected $y _ { \mathrm { C E } }$ from the set $\mathcal { V } - \{ \hat { y } \}$ at random. For the GSM8K dataset, we generated $y _ { \mathrm { C E } } = \hat { y } + \epsilon$ ，where $\epsilon$ was sampled from the uniform distribution $\operatorname { U n i f } \{ 1 , 2 , \dots , 1 0 \}$

Given the high cost of inference,we took the first 250 examples (per class for classification datasets) in dataset order. While we did not track the precise time, the experiments took several days on multiple GPUs to complete. We occasionally used ChatGPT for help with programming errors.
